defects: Replaces the specific 'second isomorphism theorem moves' relation (defined via IsMaximal x (x ⊔ y) → relates (x, x⊔y) to (x⊓y, y)) with a fully abstract, unconstrained relation `moves : Rel (Set L) (Set L)`, so the produced statement never encodes the actual second-isomorphism-theorem content and instead becomes a generic, trivial fact about Relation.EqvGen being the least equivalence relation containing any relation
Omits the JordanHolderLattice typeclass and the IsMaximal (covering) hypothesis entirely, which is essential to defining what the 'moves' are
Uses Set L (arbitrary sets) as the underlying type of the relation instead of X × X (pairs representing intervals [x, x⊔y] etc.), losing the 'intervals of a lattice' structure
Drops the specific JordanHolderLattice.Iso relation from the conclusion, replacing 'e x y' for Iso-related x y with a generic EqvGen-minimality statement for an uninterpreted moves relation

As stated, the theorem is essentially a generic/trivial fact about Relation.EqvGen (already essentially true by construction for any relation), not a formalization of the intended lattice-theoretic theorem
